A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RACTD research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original RACTD evaluations on Gym-MuJoCo and Maze2D, inference-time measurements, reward-distribution analysis and ablations in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional FrankaKitchen results, dataset-quality comparisons and sensitivity analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The EDM teacher, CTM/DSM/reward objective, frozen return predictor and sampling procedures are retained. Equations 5–9 remain equivalent. Planner terminology and the expanded reward-network description do not establish an actual algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: v2 adds FrankaKitchen partial, mixed and complete datasets, extending evaluation to robotic manipulation. Appendix D.1 also adds hopper random and expert datasets beyond the retained mixed-quality MuJoCo coverage. Maze2D remains; mentioning OGBench does not establish evaluation on that benchmark.

E2.justification: Flow Q-learning is newly included in the Maze2D comparison and the new Kitchen partial/mixed comparison (v2 Tables 3 and 2). Existing MuJoCo and fast-sampling comparator sets are retained; Flow Q-learning does not appear in the MuJoCo results table.

E3.justification: v2 adds last-epoch offline model selection alongside best-checkpoint online selection. New controlled experiments vary DSM/reward weights and observation/planning horizons. Table 9 changes the reported hopper-medium-replay reward weight from 1.0 to 0.8. These establish substantial evaluation-design changes without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds DSM-loss removal and weight sensitivity, a broader reward-weight sweep, and a joint observation/planning-horizon ablation (Tables 14, 15 and 17). Figure 4 replaces the 0.5/0.7 learning curves with a 0.8 curve. Existing teacher/student reward placement, fast-sampler and sampling-step analyses remain, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard errors over 100 planning seeds and use 20 rollouts for intermediate reward-weight learning curves. Additional results extend these reporting practices; no changed run counts or new statistical estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises RACTD's online average from 97.6 to 101.5 and adds an offline average of 96.4. Walker2d-medium changes from 98.9 to 118.8, while hopper-medium changes from 121.0 to 115.5. Kitchen, random/expert, Flow Q-learning and ablation results are added. Existing Maze2D scores and timings remain. Hopper-replay revisions accompany a reward-weight change, so they are not controlled same-setting gains; Table 10 also contains unreconciled appendix values.

T1.justification: New Appendix G adds a proof sketch connecting reward-aware distillation to off-policy deterministic policy gradients through a Taylor approximation, gradient derivation and claimed reward/Q-function equivalence. v1 contains the diffusion and CTM mathematics but no corresponding argument. This is substantial new theoretical reasoning, although its equivalence assumptions are not established.

C1.justification: The headline advantage changes from 8.7% (97.6 versus Consistency AC's 89.8 in v1) to 9.7% (96.4 versus Diffusion QL's 87.9 under v2's offline selection). The single-step and decoupled-training contributions remain, while the retained 142-fold speedup is now explicitly credited to underlying consistency trajectory distillation.

C2.justification: The sampling-step interpretation changes from improvement with diminishing gains to barely any improvement (v1 Section 5.3 versus v2 Appendix E.5). v2 adds interpretations of random/expert dataset limitations and horizon effects. The mode-selection explanation, diversity tradeoff and stated training-cost/instability limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies four Conv1D/group-normalization/Mish reward-model blocks and a linear output layer, and updates one reported reward weight. However, it omits v1 Appendix B.2's environment-specific discount factors and -100 early-termination penalty. Existing model-size tables, noise schedulers, hardware disclosure and conditional code-release promise remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Flow Q-learning, OGBench and deterministic policy gradients. It contrasts Flow Q-learning's concurrent optimization with RACTD, introduces the policy-gradient connection and more explicitly attributes acceleration to CTD. Most existing related-work coverage and positioning remain.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify planner terminology and CTD attribution, particularly in the abstract and introduction. Reward-model details receive a separate appendix, two main-text ablation subsections move to Appendix E, and an impact statement is added. Most main-section ordering and technical exposition are preserved.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reorganized into offline/online panels, six new tables present additional evaluations and ablations, and the Maze2D table gains a comparator row. Figure 4 is redrawn with different curves, legend and vertical scale and moved to the appendix. The document template and numerous table placements also change; Figures 1–3 retain their content.

improvement.justification: Last-epoch comparisons reduce reliance on online checkpoint selection, while Kitchen evaluations and targeted loss/horizon ablations make applicability and sensitivity easier to assess. These benefits are moderated by lost discount/penalty disclosures and new reliability problems: Table 10 labels Diffuser values as hopper that Table 1 assigns to Walker2d, and Appendix G does not justify equating the fixed return predictor with the current-policy Q-function. The empirical assessment improves, but these shortcomings limit the overall gain.
